name: Nodular Urticaria Pigmentosa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Cutaneous Mastocytosis

criteria.description: Presence of multiple nodular pigmented lesions with urticarial reaction on stroking (Darier's sign)
Biopsy showing dense mast cell infiltrate in the dermis
Elevated serum tryptase levels above normal range
Detection of activating KIT gene mutations in lesional skin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (clinical presentation and histopathology) or one major plus two minor criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Darier's sign is a key clinical feature; biopsy confirmation is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Darier's sign (urticarial wheal formation upon lesion stroking)
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic wheal and flare reaction on mechanical irritation
searchTerms: skin bump turns into hive on rubbing

common.symptomName: Flushing episodes triggered by heat or stress
searchTerms: flushing triggered by heat or stress

common.symptomName: Mast cell mediator-related symptoms such as headache and dizziness

imaging: Bone scintigraphy may show increased uptake in systemic involvement
other: Positive Darier's sign on physical examination
Histopathology showing dense dermal mast cell infiltrate with toluidine blue or Giemsa stain

distinguishingFeatures: Typically maculopapular lesions rather than nodular
Similar Darier's sign but different lesion morphology
Histopathology shows scattered mast cells rather than nodular aggregates
Solitary mast cell tumor rather than multiple nodules
Usually presents in infancy or early childhood

redFlags: Rapid increase in size or number of nodular lesions
Systemic symptoms such as hypotension or anaphylaxis
Elevated serum tryptase levels suggestive of systemic mastocytosis
references: Castells M. Mastocytosis: classification, diagnosis, and management. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2018.
